status: WIP: concurrent region rollback reduces measured cleanup latency by about 78%; scoped tests and mixed-workload/postchecks completed, with no stable overall throughput claim
root_cause: Rust pessimistic_rollback published one region request and synchronously waited for its completion before advancing. Pinned client-go doActionOnBatches publishes region work concurrently. The local DELIVERY tables span many regions, confirmed by the Go information_schema region map.
changes: Publish a region rollback round through the existing shared transport before completing any response.
Retain per-request publication receipts and account for successful sibling cleanup even when another request fails.
Regroup/retry region-error batches only; retain failed or ambiguous keys and their lock timestamps.

tests.green_command: cd rust && cargo test --offline --locked --release -j12 -p tidb-txnkv --test all pessimistic_lock_source::
coverage: Actual BatchCommands fixture withholds responses until both region rollback requests arrive.
Failed region retains its keys; a successful sibling is forgotten before returning the failure.
Only the region with recovery_in_progress is retried.
Existing timestamp, ForceLock conflict, partial locking and prewrite constraints remain covered.

isolation.mode: Binary prepared statements following go-tpc DELIVERY statement order; all writes rolled back. Fixed pending-order data, Go result reference, five warmups per client, rotating three-endpoint order, no profiler/build/SQL probes during timing. This is not committed TPC-C.
isolation.interpretation: Rollback mean latency improves 79.05% at one client and 77.95% at eight clients, reaching about 0.98ms versus Go 0.95-1.10ms. Whole rolled-back DELIVERY median throughput is +19.08% at one client but -2.37% at eight. Do not generalize the cleanup latency win to mixed throughput.

host_preflight: Codex renderer 63.4% CPU, WindowServer 44.5%, Codex service 11.1%; no processes stopped. Host not controlled/quiescent.

tpcc.note: Shared evolving dataset; tool RNG is time-seeded; no ignored errors or time cutoff
